title: Reenact & Expand Pistol Purchase Permit
lastAction: Ref To Com On Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill reinstates North Carolina's pistol purchase permit law that was previously repealed and expands it to require permits for long gun (rifle and shotgun) purchases as well. Under the bill, sheriffs would issue permits valid for five years after conducting background checks and assessing moral character, with exceptions for antique firearms.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this bill enhances public safety by requiring background checks and character assessments before all firearm purchases, closing what they see as a gap since the pistol permit law was repealed. They contend that expanding permits to include long guns creates a more comprehensive system to keep firearms away from dangerous individuals and those with criminal histories.
aiConArguments: Opponents argue this bill places unnecessary burdens on law-abiding citizens by requiring permits for routine firearm purchases and adds administrative costs to sheriffs' offices. They contend that existing federal background check systems for licensed dealers are sufficient, and that the vague 'good moral character' standard gives sheriffs too much discretionary power to deny permits.
